No.21

How the Bodhisattva Views Good and Evil, Right and Wrong in the World

Beyond names and labels, looking at the intention behind an action.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: how does the Bodhisattva view good and evil, right and wrong in the world?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Good and evil stand opposed
because of discrimination."
"Wrong and right depend on each other,
appearing from the mind."
"To cling to goodness as 'mine'
is already to fall into bias;
to see evil and be able to turn it
is what is called right view."

"Judge conduct by its causes,
not by its name."

🔶Plain Rendering

Labels of discrimination: what the world calls good and evil is not an absolute, unchanging truth, but labels people mark out with a discriminating mind.

Appearing from the mind: wrong and right are not two separate things, but two sides of one whole. Whatever thoughts arise in your heart, that is the kind of world that appears.

Turning toward right view: if you cling to "I am good", you have already fallen into bias; if you can see an evil thought and transform it right then, that is true right view.

The core of judgment: when looking at what people do, look at their "causes" and their "actions", not the status or the "good" or "bad" labels society gives them.
